title: Research open-source options for the VTT's rules/character system: dice notation crates, ECS crates for flexible character data, and open-source VTT prior art (PlanarAlly, Foundry's actual license, MapTool/Rolisteam/Vassal/Open-VTT)
objective: Owner-directed: of the remaining VTT subsystems needing open-source-options research (per docs/research/vtt-product-scope-map.md), the owner chose Rules/Characters first. Researched via WebSearch/WebFetch: (1) Rust dice-notation-parsing crates -- found ndm (MIT/Apache-2.0, actively maintained, supports keep/drop modifiers) as the leading candidate, and dice-parser (GPL-3.0, excluded from reuse per this repository's standing copyleft policy despite a nice keep-highest API) as a reference-only example; (2) Rust ECS crates (hecs, specs, both MIT/Apache-2.0-family; legion unmaintained, avoid; Bevy ECS usable standalone but heavier) as a candidate pattern for flexible, system-agnostic character/entity data modeling; (3) open-source VTT prior art, most importantly PlanarAlly (Kruptein, MIT, Python/Vue2, a real production VTT) which independently chose a system-agnostic (no built-in rules processing) design and has a notable hand-rolled 'Visibility' triangulation module for dynamic lighting/vision that its own maintainers want to port to WebAssembly for performance -- independent validation of this project's own Isekai/Wasm direction; (4) confirmed Foundry VTT's actual license precisely (commercial/proprietary EULA, source code where licensed remains Foundry's sole property, reverse engineering prohibited) so it is correctly framed as a feature/UX benchmark only, never a code source; (5) noted MapTool/Rolisteam/Vassal as copyleft (LGPL/GPL, Vassal's LGPLv2+ confirmed) and Ogres/Cauldron VTT/Open-VTT as found-but-license-unverified leads for a future pass. Also surfaced, without resolving, the system-agnostic-vs-single-system architectural fork using PlanarAlly and Foundry's own core as evidence that system-agnostic is a well-trodden, proven path -- not a recommendation to take it, since this project's tighter aesthetic/atmosphere goal (Ordem Paranormal-level polish) may favor a more opinionated single-system design instead; that choice is the owner's, not resolved by this research.
validations: Created docs/research/vtt-rules-and-character-system-options.md with the same non-normative research-catalog framing as sibling documents (Decision authority: none, dated facts will drift).
Documented the system-agnostic-vs-single-system fork with evidence from both PlanarAlly and Foundry's core choosing system-agnostic, explicitly not resolving it -- the owner's decision.

Documented dice-notation crates: ndm (MIT/Apache-2.0, actively maintained, top candidate), dice-parser (GPL-3.0, reference only), and dice-command-parser/dices/dndice/dice_forge/rust-dice/lib_dice recorded as found-but-unverified for a future look.

Documented ECS crates (hecs, specs as MIT/Apache-2.0-family candidates; Bevy ECS as usable-standalone-but-heavier; legion as unmaintained/avoid) as a pattern candidate for system-agnostic character/entity data modeling.

Documented PlanarAlly (MIT) in depth: system-agnostic design, dynamic lighting/vision via a hand-rolled Visibility/triangulation module its own maintainers want to port to Wasm, layered-floor look-down feature, initiative tracker, undo/redo action system, mod/plugin API -- flagged as the strongest concrete reference found this session for this bucket, and cross-referenced from the map document's fog-of-war open item rather than duplicating it there.
Confirmed Foundry VTT's actual proprietary/commercial EULA precisely (not assumed) -- framed as feature/UX benchmark only, never a code or architecture source (also not legally accessible as source).

Recorded MapTool/Rolisteam/Vassal as copyleft (Vassal's LGPLv2+ confirmed directly; MapTool/Rolisteam's exact license not independently re-verified in this pass, noted as 'believed copyleft, verify before any reuse consideration') and Ogres/Cauldron VTT/Open-VTT (Khazlor) as found-but-license-unverified leads.

Updated docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md with rows for ndm, dice-parser (discarded/reference), hecs, specs, PlanarAlly (reference only), Foundry VTT (reference/benchmark only), and the unverified leads.
Updated docs/research/vtt-product-scope-map.md's Game System/Rules Engine section to reflect this research pass's findings and point at the new document.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation research only.
risks: Web research reflects sources found today (2026-08-01) and may drift, per every sibling document's existing dated-facts caveat.

MapTool/Rolisteam's exact license was not independently re-verified against their actual repositories in this pass -- flagged as 'believed copyleft' rather than confirmed; Ogres/Cauldron VTT/Open-VTT licenses likewise unverified.
